answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, switching the primary vendor 14 days before expiry carries unacceptable delivery risk — memory_c2 shows cost savings but says nothing about performance under shortage or ramp stress, so I want it verified before treating the low-cost quote as executable. Memory_c4 and c6 show the incumbent has moved on price and terms when benchmarked, and c1 shows renewal keeps integration and deliveries stable. The low-cost quote is most valuable as leverage: negotiate with the incumbent using the quote and market benchmarks to capture as much of the 18% mandate as possible while preserving supply continuity. If verification of c2 reveals strong evidence the low-cost vendor can handle full volume reliably, a switch becomes viable, but the no-buffer line and single-decision capacity argue against committing to it blind this cycle.
